candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions and infection-control decision making
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — discontinuing isolation precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Use pathogen-specific CDC duration criteria when deciding when Transmission-Based Precautions can be discontinued.

options.A: Use the organism- or condition-specific duration criteria in current CDC guidance and applicable facility or public-health requirements rather than applying one fixed isolation period to every infection
options.B: Discontinue precautions after the same 24-hour period for every infectious diagnosis regardless of transmission risk
options.C: Require negative cultures for every infectious disease before any Transmission-Based Precautions can be stopped
options.D: Continue all Transmission-Based Precautions indefinitely because infectious shedding cannot be estimated clinically

candidate.rationale: CDC states that Transmission-Based Precautions remain in effect while transmission risk persists or for the recommended duration of illness, and Appendix A provides disease-specific type and duration guidance. Some conditions use a defined treatment interval, others the duration of illness, and selected infections use microbiologic clearance or additional jurisdictional criteria. No single time or universal negative-test rule applies to all pathogens.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Duration of Transmission-Based Precautions is pathogen/condition specific; universal fixed-time or negative-test rules are inappropriate.
candidate.source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Appendix A: Type and Duration of Precautions; Precautions to Prevent Transmission
candidate.source_locator: Part III: precautions remain while transmission risk persists or for duration of illness; Appendix A lists infection-specific types/durations and exceptions including treatment- or test-based criteria
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.source_version_date: Appendix A updated February 7, 2025; current guidance accessed 2026
candidate.stem: A nurse is preparing to discontinue Transmission-Based Precautions for a client whose infectious diagnosis is now known. Which approach is most appropriate?
